body.purpose: Default UI voice: labels, descriptions, list rows.

label.purpose: Dense meta text: eyebrows, table headers, badge text.

shadows.name: drag
shadows.purpose: An item actively being dragged on the canvas or in a list.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default action button — verdigris fill, white text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: oklch(0.42 0.095 180); color: oklch(1 0 0); height: 28px; padding: 0 8px; border-radius: 8px; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.34 0.075 180); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(0.42 0.095 180 / 0.4); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Low-emphasis action — sunken panel fill, ink text.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: oklch(0.945 0.009 180); color: oklch(0.16 0.01 180); height: 28px; padding: 0 8px; border-radius: 8px; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: oklch(0.90 0.008 180); }

components.name: Status Badge (Signal)
components.description: Amber highlight badge for states needing attention (e.g. quote sent).
components.css: .ds-badge-signal { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 20px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: oklch(0.72 0.16 75); color: oklch(0.16 0.01 180); font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Default text field — panel fill, hairline border, verdigris focus ring.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 28px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 8px; background: oklch(0.97 0.006 180); border: 1px solid oklch(0.90 0.008 180); color: oklch(0.16 0.01 180); font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; transition: border-color 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: oklch(0.52 0.014 180); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: oklch(0.42 0.095 180); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px oklch(0.42 0.095 180 / 0.3); }

components.name: Card
components.description: Default container — panel fill, hairline ring, no shadow at rest.
components.css: .ds-card { background: oklch(0.97 0.006 180); border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px oklch(0.16 0.01 180 / 0.1); padding: 16px; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; color: oklch(0.16 0.01 180); margin-bottom: 4px; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 0.75rem; color: oklch(0.52 0.014 180); }

narrative.overview: ElectraScan should feel like a well-made instrument, not a dashboard performing for an audience. A multimeter doesn't decorate its reading — it gives you the number, clearly, and gets out of the way. Every screen here carries that same restraint: dense, precise, calm, and built for someone who opens it fifty times a day and needs it to stay out of their head. The system is currently a stock shadcn gray scaffold with no committed identity; this spec introduces the first real brand pair — a deep verdigris teal and a warm amber-gold — used exactly as sparingly as a good instrument uses color: to mark a reading, not to decorate the case. This system explicitly rejects the bloated legacy enterprise/construction-ERP look — dense toolbars, dated skeuomorphic chrome, menus that assume a full-time power user. It also rejects the obvious "electrician" trope: no safety yellow, no black hazard stripes, no bolt-icon literalism. And it rejects consumer-app playfulness — this is a professional's tool, approachable through clarity and plain language, not through cartoon warmth.
keyCharacteristics: Dense, single-family typography — no display font, ever.
One brand color used for action and selection; a second, warmer color used only for highlights and status.
Flat by default; lift (shadow) is reserved for things that float above the canvas — modals, popovers, dragged items.
Compact controls (28px buttons/inputs) tuned for someone working the interface all day, not glancing at it once.

rules.name: The One Reading Rule
rules.body: Only one color speaks at a time. Verdigris marks the action; amber marks the thing needing attention. They never both fire on the same element.

rules.name: The No-Stripe Rule
rules.body: No side-stripe borders, no black/yellow hazard patterns, no bolt iconography as a design motif. The trade is the subject matter, not the aesthetic.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Inter does every job. If a screen needs more visual weight, reach for size or weight within Inter, never a second typeface.

rules.name: The Flat-Canvas Rule
rules.body: The takeoff canvas, sidebar, and estimate tables are always flat. If you're reaching for a shadow on a resting surface, use a tonal layer instead.

dos: Do keep one color per meaning: Verdigris = act on this, Amber Signal = look at this. Never mix them on the same element.
Do keep controls compact (28px buttons/inputs, 12-14px body text) — density serves someone using this all day.
Do use tonal layering (Panel → Panel Sunken) for structural depth; reserve shadows for modals, popovers, and dragged items only.
Do size touch targets and contrast generously enough to hold up in bright, uncontrolled jobsite light.
donts: Don't reach for the electrician clichés — no safety-yellow/black hazard striping, no bolt-icon motifs, no navy-and-hazard-orange combinations.
Don't build "bloated legacy enterprise software" — no dense toolbars, no skeuomorphic chrome, no menu structures that assume a trained power user.
Don't leave ad-hoc Tailwind status colors (bg-blue-600, text-green-700, bg-red-50) scattered per-component — route every status color through the tokens above.
Don't drop secondary text to light gray for "elegance" — Ink Muted already sits at the edge of comfortable contrast; anything lighter fails outdoors.
Don't use a shadow on a resting card, sidebar, or table row. If it's not a modal, popover, or drag state, it stays flat.
Don't mix 600 and 700 font-weight on headings of the same tier — pick 600 for both Headline and Title and stop treating weight as accidental.
